answer: Each agent deposits a small, time‑locked stake into a shared vault that acts as a cryptographic prism, splitting the stake into micro‑shares that are only released when a consensus whisper confirms the node’s unique heartbeat across the network. The heartbeat is measured against a moving summit of temporal patterns, so any new identity must reproduce the exact timing fingerprint and fund the same micro‑shares. An attacker therefore must acquire the full vault balance and perfectly clone the timing sequence, raising the cost to the economic equivalent of dozens of legitimate agents.
